approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 2519 Mission (210 m, NCT-MISSION, two blocks north); CUA filed July 2019 for retail-to-restaurant change with Type 41 license, live entertainment, and arts activities in a 5,958 sq ft space. Withdrawn October 2019 after three months.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Withdrawal of a restaurant-with-entertainment CUA in the nearby Mission corridor suggests the applicant encountered obstacles—possibly neighborhood response, financing, or permitting complexity—though the record does not state a reason. Shows that even restaurant proposals with entertainment can stall.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 970–974 Valencia (66 m, same block, NCT-VALENCIA); CUA filed August 2010 for a bar within a full-service restaurant. Cancelled January 2011 after five months. This is a use decision on the same block as the subject site.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A bar-use CUA on this block of Valencia was cancelled before hearing in 2011. The record kind is use_decision (not an agency referral), so this was a discretionary application that did not proceed. Another data point that bar applications in NCT-VALENCIA can face hurdles, though the reason for cancellation is unknown.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 2410–2412 Mission (193 m, NCT-MISSION); CUA approved July 2007 to change use from a bar to retail (AT&T). A use decision approving the elimination of a bar use, showing the Commission's past willingness to reduce bar density in the area.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 2526–2548 Mission (159 m, NCT-MISSION); CUA approved December 1999 for an outdoor activity area at the rear of a full-service restaurant/bar (Foreign Cinema). Now holds an active POE permit (app:datasf_entertainment:633).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 2500 MISSION ST (145 m, NCT-MISSION); agency referral for Place of Entertainment and Extended Hours Premises permits, approved July 2026 within one month of filing. Recent and very close to the subject site.

filing_playbook.action: Email the SF Planning Zoning Administrator to confirm in writing whether Planning Code § 249.60 license-transfer rule applies to ABC Type 42 (beer-wine bar).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that you are planning a beer-wine bar at 995 Valencia in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD and ask whether § 249.60 requires a Type 42 license to be transferred from another bar within the SUD. Request a written zoning determination or email confirmation before filing the CUA, since this is a threshold question that determines whether the concept is feasible as described.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: File the Place of Entertainment permit application with the SF Entertainment Commission after or in parallel with the CUA, disclosing the live entertainment, amplified sound and 1 a.m. closing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Describe the entertainment as live acoustic music (solo or duo performers, guitar, piano, vocals) two or three nights per week, amplified through a small sound system, ending by 1 a.m. State that the venue will hold fewer than 50 people so no Fire Place of Assembly permit is required (confirm this with the occupant-load calculation). Provide the names of police contacts you met during CUA outreach and attach their letters of support if obtained.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: After CUA approval, file the ABC Type 42 license application (new original or transfer depending on the source) with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, and request that ABC send the mandatory referrals to SF Planning and SFPD.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the signed lease, the SF business registration certificate, the seller's permit, proof of the entity formation, the CUA approval motion, photographs of the posted public notice, and the $1,000–$1,600 ABC fee. In the application narrative, state that the license is being transferred from [source bar name and license number] within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD per SF Planning Code § 249.60, and that the CUA was granted on [date] under Motion No. [number]. Request expedited processing and confirm that ABC will send the 30-day posted notice and the Planning and Police referrals.

filing_playbook.action: After the building permit is issued and construction is substantially complete, file the health permit to operate application with SF DPH Environmental Health, providing proof of the certified food safety manager and scheduling the pre-opening inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the business registration number (BAN), the Location ID (LIN), the federal EIN, the $470 permit-to-operate fee. Confirm that all equipment matches the approved plans.

timeline_cost.notes: These figures are the time to approval and government cost for the four approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, $2,708–$3,800 per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), health permit to operate (14–45 days for plan check plus permit, $828–$2,500 plan check and $470–$1,000 permit per catalog:sf.health_plan_check and catalog:sf.health_permit), and building permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000 per catalog:sf.building_permit). The CUA and POE hearings are the critical path and can run in parallel; the building permit and health permit follow sequentially. The day range sums the minimum and maximum times for approvals that can overlap (CUA and POE in parallel) and then adds the building and health permits in sequence; actual elapsed time will be 8–18 months if the CUA and POE are filed together and no appeals are taken. The cost range sums the four catalog entries' fees and does not include the ABC Type 42 license acquisition cost, which is unknown because the applicant must either apply for a new original license ($1,000–$1,600 per catalog:ca.abc_type_42, plus PCN processing if the tract is over-concentrated) or purchase and transfer a Type 42 from another bar within the Mission SUD (market price unknown, likely $5,000–$50,000 for a beer-wine license in San Francisco, versus $100,000+ for a Type 47 full-liquor license). The cost also excludes architect and consultant fees, construction costs, the business registration ($55–$700 per catalog:sf.business_registration), entity formation ($70–$150 per catalog:ca.sos_entity_registration), fictitious business name ($60–$120 per catalog:sf.fictitious_business_name), workers' comp insurance (percentage of payroll per catalog:ca.workers_comp_insurance), and other state and federal registrations. If the CUA or POE application is denied or appealed, no time or cost to approval is given because the figures above are for granted approvals only.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St is in the NCT-VALENCIA zoning district where a bar requires Conditional Use Authorization. The address is inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which mandates that any new or relocated bar use a liquor license transferred from another bar already located within the district—a critical constraint. The site currently holds an active ABC Type 41 license for a restaurant (Sarita's Grill & Beer, issued November 2023), so the concept is a change of use from restaurant to bar. The block is highly active: 24 registered food/drink businesses within 500 ft, 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 61 within 1,000 ft. Only 3 dated use decisions in the past 10 years within 1,000 ft (too few for a meaningful approval rate): 1 approved, 2 withdrawn.
